body: Joe Wallach, an executive who helped form the Rede Globo media network, has died. His death was reported in the Journal Anhanguera 1st Edition Saturday November 21 2026.
Severe storms, described as supercells, caused damage in 36 cities in Rio Grande do Sul according to Civil Defense. The death toll in Tupanciretã has risen to four.
en.context: The Journal Anhanguera 1st Edition Saturday November 21 2026 covered national stories including the death of a media executive, severe weather in southern Brazil, and political developments in Argentina regarding disability rights.

body: Joe Wallach, ein leitender Angestellter, der bei der Gründung des Mediennetzwerks Rede Globo mitwirkte, ist gestorben. Sein Tod wurde im Journal Anhanguera 1. Auflage am Samstag, 21. November 2026, berichtet.

Heftige Stürme, die als Superzellen beschrieben wurden, verursachten in 36 Städten in Rio Grande do Sul Schäden, so die Zivilschutzbehörde. Die Zahl der Todesopfer in Tupanciretã ist auf vier gestiegen.
de.context: Das Journal Anhanguera 1. Auflage Samstag, 21. November 2026 berichtete über nationale Geschichten einschließlich des Todes eines Medienmanagers, schwerem Wetter im südlichen Brasilien und politischen Entwicklungen in Argentinien bezüglich Behindertenrechte.

Des orages violents, qualifiés de supercells, ont causé des dégâts dans 36 villes du Rio Grande do Sul selon la Défense civile. Le bilan humain à Tupanciretã s'est élevé à quatre morts.

ko.title: 영상: 안하구에라 1면 토요일 2026년 11월 21일

리우그란두두술 호우로 36개 시·군 피해

body: 조 월라치, 레데 글로보 미디어 네트워크 설립에 기여한 임원, 별세했다. 그의 사망 소식은 2026년 11월 21일자 저널 안하구에라 1면에서 전해졌다.
민방위(Civil Defense) 발표에 따르면 슈퍼셀로 불리는 강력한 뇌우가 리우그란데두술 주 36개 도시에 피해를 입혔다. 투파니레타(Tupanciretã) 사망자 수가 4명으로 늘었다.
ko.context: 안하구에라 1면 토요일 2026년 11월 21일 호는 언론인 사망, 남부 브라질 호우, 아르헨티나 장애인 권리 정치 개발을 다룬 국가 뉴스를 다뤘다.

problemsFixed: Invented claim: 'Joe Wallach, co-founder of Rede Globo' — source only says 'Morre Joe Wallach, executivo que ajudou a formar a Rede Globo' (died, executive who helped form Rede Globo). No claim of co-founding.

Invented claim: 'Severe storms, described as supercells' — source says 'Supercélula Temporais' but does not say they caused damage in 36 cities; it says 'causaram estragos em 36 cidades' (caused damage in 36 cities). The 'supercell' label is not in the source and adds unverified detail.
Invented claim: 'Death toll in Tupanciretã rises to four' — source says 'Sobe para quatro o número de mortos em Tupanciretã' (rises to four dead in Tupanciretã). This is supported.

Invented claim: 'Video footage shows destruction trail' — source has 'VÍDEO: Imagens aéreas mostram rastro de destruição' (VIDEO: aerial images show destruction trail). This is supported but must be attributed.

Invented claim: 'Brazilian President Moraes authorizes daily visits' — source says 'Hospital em Brasília Moraes autoriza visitas diárias de filhos a Bolsonaro em hospital' (Moraes authorizes daily visits to Bolsonaro in hospital). Supported but must attribute Moraes.

Body paragraph 3: Invented content about Argentina disability resolution — source S2 is about Argentina disability policy but the draft's claim about 'resolution naming people with disabilities using derogatory terms' and 'Pope Francis visited' is a patchwork of S2 quotes and unsynthesized claims. The draft does not correctly attribute S2 claims.
Facts list includes claims not in sources (e.g. 'Joe Wallach, co-founder').
Body: 'Severe storms, described as supercells' — unverified adjective.
